---
title: "Mathematical detail"
---

Formulas used by `CampbellCochraneModel`. Notation follows Campbell and
Cochrane (1999). The solver runs monthly; reported moments are
annualized.

## Surplus

Habit $X_t$ is external. Surplus consumption is $S_t=(C_t-X_t)/C_t$,
$s_t=\log S_t$. Consumption growth is i.i.d.,
$\Delta c_{t+1}=g+v_{t+1}$, $v\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$. Log surplus is

$$
s_{t+1}=(1-\phi)\bar s+\phi s_t+\lambda(s_t)\,v_{t+1}.
$$

Steady-state surplus is $\bar S=\sigma\sqrt{\gamma/(1-\phi)}$. The
sensitivity that keeps the bill locally constant ($b=0$) is

$$
\lambda(s)=\frac{1}{\bar S}\sqrt{1-2(s-\bar s)}-1
\quad\text{for }s\le s_{\max}=\bar s+\tfrac12(1-\bar S^2),
$$

and $\lambda(s)=0$ above $s_{\max}$.

## Kernel

$$
M_{t+1}=\delta G_{t+1}^{-\gamma}e^{-\gamma(s_{t+1}-s_t)},
\qquad G_{t+1}=e^{\Delta c_{t+1}}.
$$

$\delta$ is set so the bill at $\bar s$ equals the annual 0.94 percent
target of the paper.

## Consumption claim

The price-consumption ratio $P/C(s)$ solves

$$
\frac{P}{C}(s)=E\left[M'\,G'\left(1+\frac{P'}{C'}\right)\Bigm|s\right]
$$

on a grid for $s$, with Gauss-Hermite integration over $v$. Equity
return is $G'(1+P'/C')/(P/C)$. The bill is $1/E[M\mid s]$. Annual
returns are the product of twelve monthly gross returns.

Source: Campbell and Cochrane (1999).
